clue.text: Tom and Jerry perform to tease the 10

definitions.note: the 1913 law let hunger-striking suffragettes out of prison and rearrested them, toying with them

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, as in the cartoon pair
Jerry is the cartoon mouse who torments Tom
to perform is to act

explanation.surface: The famous cartoon duo put on a show to taunt the protesting women.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prisoners (Temporary Discharge for Ill-Health) Act 1913 was nicknamed after the game a cat plays with a mouse: freed hunger strikers were re-jailed once fit. '10' is the suffragettes of 10 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of a British law aimed at suffragettes, released and rearrested in a teasing cycle like a cat's game with its prey.

clue.text: Entice director to include maverick's part in realistic style

indicators.note: to include means the rearranged letters wrap round another piece
a director arranges things, so the letters of the word before it are put in a fresh order
only part of the word is used, its last two letters dropped

parts.note: the word maverick is the source of the part used

explanation.surface: Tempt a film director to put in a bit of a rebel's character for a gritty, true-to-life look.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog called this clue weak: 'director' is a noun, an unusual anagram signal, and 'maverick's part' gives a lopped word rather than a clean piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinéma vérité is a documentary film style aiming at naturalism and unstaged realism.

clue.text: Call in case

definitions.meaning: a ... call is an old term for a long-distance telephone call
a large travelling case or chest

explanation.definitionFit: Trunk names both a long-distance phone call (trunk call) and a big luggage box.

clue.text: Ban on Blair's journey — can't start without plates — an absolute refusal

parts.note: a ban is a no
Tony Blair, the former Prime Minister; his memoir is called A Journey

indicators.note: without here means outside, wrapping round another piece
the word cannot begin, so its first letter goes

parts.note: L-plates are the learner plates on a British learner driver's car, so two Ls

explanation.surface: A prohibition on the former PM's travels: unable to get going without learner plates, the answer is a flat no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't start' turns journey into OURNEY, and 'without' puts it round LL. L-plates are the red L signs a British learner driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom is an emphatic, colloquial way of refusing outright.

clue.text: Bad name envelops celebrity that's keen

indicators.note: envelops means wraps round, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: someone whose name is mud has a bad reputation
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A notorious reputation surrounds a famous person who is enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your name is mud' is the idiom behind MUD.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang from 'keen as mustard': mustard can mean eager or enthusiastic.

clue.text: Discloses international body's overheads

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations, an international body
locks are hair, which grows over heads

explanation.surface: A global organisation reveals its running costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overheads' looks like business costs; here it is the hair on top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlock a secret is to open it up, reveal or disclose it.

clue.text: I don't feature in either solvent or anaesthetic

indicators.note: the letter named is left out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone protests they play no part in either of two chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a volatile liquid used as a solvent and formerly as a general anaesthetic.

clue.text: Fish outside ancient British student circle and what circulates in it

indicators.note: outside means the fish's letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: cod is a fish
ancient means old
L is a learner, a student
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A fish swims round an old British student society, and something flows through its veins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the fish: fish are cold-blooded, so cold blood circulates in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish are cold-blooded animals, so the fluid in their veins can be called cold blood.

clue.text: Ancient relative in China until recently

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: An elderly family member was living in China until not long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recently' is only padding for the surface, as the blog notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Naunt is an archaic form of aunt, from 'mine aunt' misdivided.

clue.text: Where Midlanders are broaching the Solent, not with a catamaran?

indicators.note: broaching is opening up or beginning, so only the start of the strait is taken

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England
a catamaran has two hulls; a monohull has one: I (one) HULL

explanation.surface: West Midlands folk sailing into the Solent, but not aboard a twin-hulled boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broaching' gives the opening SOL of Solent; the blog doubted this. Solihull is a town in the West Midlands of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Solihull is a town near Birmingham in the West Midlands, home to Midlanders.

clue.text: Would-be electors of small county fashion upstanding animals' home

parts.note: Suff. is the short form of Suffolk, an English county
the rage is the fashion

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: Voters of a little shire make stylish an upright creature's lair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' turns SETT into TTES. Suffolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffragettes campaigned for women's right to vote: they sought to become electors.

clue.text: Man with neck broken for introducing 1 across

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A fellow with an injured neck is credited for bringing in a law.
explanation.walkthrough: Reginald McKenna was the Home Secretary who brought in the 1913 Act of 1 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Reginald McKenna, Home Secretary, is known for introducing the 1913 law nicknamed after a cat's game.

clue.text: Reindeer's vehicle one nearly has a fight with

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A reindeer's sleigh is almost involved in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribou is the North American name for the reindeer.

clue.text: Name of explorer No 5 when with company

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
as can mean when

explanation.surface: The fifth explorer named, when travelling with a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Vasco da Gama, the Portuguese navigator, has this as his first name.

clue.text: A little drop of make-up required?

parts.note: a little is short
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A tiny bit of cosmetics is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics; it is what must be made up to cover a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is a deficit, the amount that must be made up.

clue.text: Evidence of the French saint, first to be hermetically sealed?

indicators.note: first says the French and saint pieces come before the evidence

parts.note: du is French for of the
evidence is proof

explanation.surface: Proof concerning a French saint, the first to be canonised behind airtight seals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hermetically sealed keeps out dust, so it is impervious to dust.

clue.text: Leader of 10 went to prison, exchanging knight for rook in one

indicators.note: exchanging shows one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Parkhurst is a prison on the Isle of Wight
R is the chess notation for rook
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: The suffragette leader was jailed, swapping chess pieces inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of Parkhurst becomes N, using chess abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmeline Pankhurst led the British suffragette movement.

clue.text: Gain order in order with border

indicators.note: in order is a signal that the letters must be put into a new order

explanation.surface: Bring about tidiness in arranging an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The river forms much of the frontier between the USA and Mexico.

clue.text: Six counties thus (as with fan) must have a capital

parts.note: Northern Ireland, NI, comprises six counties
così is Italian for thus, as in Mozart's opera Così fan tutte

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland, so it seems, must possess a principal city.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket points to the opera title so that 'thus' is read in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Specify application by listener to gospel

parts.note: an ear is what listens
Mark is one of the four Gospels

explanation.surface: A request heard by someone attentive to scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark funds is to designate them for a particular use.

clue.text: Russian girl of Grenadian extraction

indicators.note: extraction means letters drawn out from within the word

explanation.surface: A Russian girl whose family comes from Grenada.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia is a Russian girl's name, short for Nadezhda.

clue.text: A huge loss

definitions.meaning: the liner that sank in 1912 was a famous loss

explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' is a link; the blog notes it makes this less than a pure double definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means enormous, and the Titanic is the great liner lost in 1912.

clue.text: See 3
Find new home for the lady back on river

indicators.note: back means read backwards

parts.note: her refers to the lady
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Rehome the woman returning to the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehouse is to give someone new accommodation.

clue.text: Shadow leader missing, unable to talk to the Sun

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, is missing

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: An opposition chief absent, unable to speak to the tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shadow leader' looks like opposition politics; 'Shadow' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbra is Latin for shadow, the darkest part of a shadow in an eclipse.

clue.text: Enough about the sick being sent back by catapult

indicators.note: about means wrapped round

parts.note: basta is Italian for enough

indicators.note: something sent back goes the way it came, so the word for the sick is read right to left

parts.note: the sick are ill

explanation.surface: Enough of the sick being hurled back by a siege engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballista was an ancient siege engine, a giant catapult or crossbow.

clue.text: Nonsense about Russian river by unthinking functionary

indicators.note: about in the sense of around, so the river's letters sit inside the word for nonsense

parts.note: rot is nonsense
the Ob is a river in Siberia

explanation.surface: Rubbish about a Russian river from a mindless official.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a person who works mechanically without thought.

clue.text: Drama of justice minister having to remove slips from pile

parts.note: a drama is a play
Jack Straw was the UK Justice Secretary; 'of' gives the possessive S

explanation.surface: A play about the justice secretary obliged to take slips off a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: Jackstraws is the game of pick-up sticks: removing straws one by one from a heap without disturbing the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing jackstraws means lifting sticks from a heap one at a time without moving others.
